title: Replicating CAPA Error-Correlation on a Safety Benchmark Across Open Models

original_idea.body:
# Replicating CAPA Error-Correlation on a Safety Benchmark Across Open Models

**Problem:** Great Models Think Alike introduced CAPA and found larger models share more errors, but on general capability benchmarks. Whether the trend holds on safety/refusal classification is untested.

**Direction:** Take a public safety classification dataset and run ~10 open models as binary classifiers. Compute CAPA on their error patterns and plot CAPA against accuracy/size.

**Why it matters:** If safety classifiers share errors that grow with capability, using one model to oversee another is fundamentally fragile.

**Relevant context:** Great Models Think Alike / CAPA (arXiv:2502.04313); Correlated Errors (arXiv:2506.07962).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (correlated safety-classifier errors -> fragile oversight) but a replication on a new domain, impact incremental.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Binary classification with a published metric (CAPA) and public dataset; very tractable for a beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: compute CAPA on a safety dataset, plot vs size; clear success criterion.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models/data, externally doable; oversight-fragility evidence labs underpublish.

novelty.reasoning: Direct method replication in a new (safety) domain; partly novel but derivative.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: CAPA method published; safety-domain application is the open slice.
